errors.evidence: The x-axis tick labels shown are 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3; there is no 10^0 label. Also the first x-value is around 4, not 3.

errors.text_span: The y-axis represents the accuracy (ACC) as a percentage on a linear scale, ranging from 40% to 65%, with tick labels at 5% intervals.
errors.evidence: The visible y-axis extends slightly below 40% (to about 37%) and slightly above 65% (to about 67%), though the tick labels are at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65.
MEMIT is plotted with purple pentagon markers, not triangle markers.

errors.text_span: The MEMIT model starts at approximately 41% and rises to around 55%.
errors.evidence: The purple MEMIT line starts at about 43.5% and ends at about 54.5%, not 41% to 55%.

errors.evidence: Base starts around 38% and ends around 44% in the figure, not 39% to 45%.

errors.text_span: The IKE model starts at roughly 43% and ends at approximately 50%.

errors.text_span: The MEND model begins at around 45% and increases to about 57%.

errors.evidence: ROME starts around 51% and ends around 66%, but the final point is closer to 66.1%; this is an approximate rounding issue.

errors.text_span: All models exhibit an overall increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
errors.evidence: Base is nearly flat from about 44% to 44% at the last two points rather than clearly increasing throughout; the statement overgeneralizes the trends.
